source_caption:
Tulsa King (2022) is a crime drama series following Dwight “The General” Manfredi, a New York Mafia capo who is released from prison after 25 years and sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma to establish a new criminal operation.
Far from the world he once knew, Dwight quickly realizes that Tulsa has its own rules. With no established crew and few connections, he begins building his operation from scratch while dealing with local criminals, unexpected allies, and people who underestimate him.
As his influence grows, Dwight finds himself caught between his new life in Tulsa and the Mafia organization that sent him there. His ambition brings money and power, but it also creates enemies and puts the people around him at risk.
The series explores themes of loyalty, ambition, family, power, identity, and starting over. Dwight may be an experienced gangster, but the world around him has changed during his decades in prison, forcing him to adapt to a new generation.
What makes Tulsa King compelling is the contrast between Dwight's old-school Mafia mentality and his unfamiliar surroundings. He is trying to build an empire while also figuring out what kind of life he wants after losing so many years.
More than just a crime story, Tulsa King follows a man trying to rebuild his influence while confronting the consequences of his past.
💬 After losing 25 years, can Dwight build an empire that truly belongs to him?

source_details.synopsis: Tulsa King is an American comedy and crime drama television series created by Taylor Sheridan for the streaming platform Paramount+. The series stars Sylvester Stallone as Dwight "The General" Manfredi, an American Mafia caporegime who has been recently released from prison in New York and is sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where he begins to set up a criminal organization. It is Stallone's first leading role in a scripted television series. The series also stars Andrea Savage, Martin Starr, Jay Will, Max Casella, Domenick Lombardozzi, Vincent Piazza, A. C.
